dishes.name: Barbagiuan
dishes.description: Barbajuan (also spelled barbagiuan or barbagiuai) is an appetizer mainly found in the eastern part of the French Riviera, in the western part of Liguria and in Monaco. A kind of fritter stuffed with Swiss chard, rice and ricotta, among other ingredients.

dishes.name: Socca
dishes.description: Socca is a small-sided team sports variant of association football, best known in 6-a-side 40-minute format. It is also played in a 7-a-side format. The International Socca Federation (ISF) is a governing body for Socca.

ingredients: Black pepper to taste; 2–3 decent grinds of a grinder should do
steps: Heat oven as high as it can go—around 300°C / 570°F is traditional, but do whatever your oven can manage that gets close to this. If using a cast-iron pan, get it into the oven at the start so that it is hot when the batter goes into it.
Whisk all the ingredients together well, ensuring there are no lumps. This should make a very thin, easy-to-pour batter.

Once the oven is up to temperature, pour some of the batter into the hot pan or onto the plaque, and put into the oven for 8–9 minutes at 300°C / 570°F, or 13–15 minutes at 250°C / 480°F. With a 50 cm plaque or pan, cook half the batter at a time—the batter should cover the plaque or pan very thinly.
Remove from the oven and cut into triangular wedges. Serve hot.
Repeat for the rest of the batter.

dishes.name: Pissaladière
dishes.description: Pissaladière is a dish of flatbread with toppings from the region of Provence and the French city of Nice. It is often compared to pizza.

dishes.name: Pan bagnat
dishes.description: The pan bagnat (pan bagna, and alternatively in French as pain bagnat) is a sandwich that is a specialty of Nice, France.

dishes.name: Fougasse monégasque
dishes.description: In French cuisine, fougasse is a type of bread typically associated with Provence but found (with variations) in other regions. Some versions are sculpted or slashed into a pattern resembling a head of wheat.
